reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, so the antibody-making cells may use them to make antibodies.
expectation: The cells will make antibodies from the amino acids.

effect: The cells made antibodies whose tips match the bacteria's surface knobs.
reaction: The matching shapes make the next step clear.
reason: The goal is to coat bacteria, and the antibody tips match their surface knobs.
expectation: The antibodies will attach to and coat the bacteria.

effect: The antibodies attached to the bacteria, completing the coating goal; immune memory still needs to be given to the body.
reaction: The matching shapes worked as expected.

expectation: The body will retain the memory lymphocytes.

effect: The body now contains memory lymphocytes, which can help produce a faster, larger antibody response if the same antigen returns. Both goals are complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to see how the first response could help later.

mostWorthwhile.text: Using the lymph node to grow descendants was most worthwhile: it showed how one activated cell leads to both antibody-making and memory cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: Coating the bacteria was clear but predictable once the matching shapes had been shown.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the same response produced both antibody-making cells and lasting memory cells.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary. The pictures and earlier protein-building idea gave the pairings a purpose.

continue.text: I would probably continue: the final result made me curious about what happens when the same antigen returns.
